correctness.rationale: The explicit graph edge sets and 2-independence definitions have independently implemented subset enumeration and direct connectivity checks on all 65,536 subsets per graph. All 1192/1336 nonempty faces and 543/639 facet-cover matches are constructed in the included source code. The directed Hasse graphs (4224/4960 relations) are exhaustively topologically ordered; therefore both matchings are acyclic. Remaining critical cells are one vertex and 105/57 cells of dimension three only. The discrete-Morse CW theorem then gives wedges of 105/57 three-spheres integrally, with no attaching-map ambiguity because there are no intervening cells. Independent mod-two homology agrees but is not used in place of the integral homotopy proof.

originality.rationale: The closest published same-graph comparison is ordinary 1-independence, which does not logically determine 2-independence. Inspected full primary research documents cover trees, complete multipartite/fully whiskered graphs, cycles, paths and specified shellable constructions, not these two strongly regular graphs. Six targeted published-record queries and eight text searches for aliases and numbers returned no covering theorem/table. Remaining risks include unindexed equivalent work and unread full text of the close ordinary-independence record; no claim of absolute priority is made.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande and 4x4 rook graphs form a mathematically natural, canonical pair of nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs with identical parameters. A full integral homotopy classification for the first higher-independence parameter is a meaningful finite benchmark and shows that their higher-independence topological types differ strongly (ranks 57 versus 105), beyond the previously studied r=1 case. The finding includes exhaustive reproducible exact acyclic matchings and determines full homotopy, not just a small sampled invariant.
